issues.legal_issue: Criminal proceedings should not be quashed when the complaint and supporting material prima facie disclose the ingredients of offences and the accused’s defenses depend on disputed facts for trial.
material_facts: The complaint alleged that the accused inflicted injuries, attempted to strike the complainant on the head with an iron rod, and threatened to kill the complainant.
The Magistrate-recorded statements, together with the complaint, were found to disclose the ingredients of the offences charged.
The accused relied on pending civil disputes and a prior criminal complaint to argue that the complaint was a counterblast, and disputed whether one accused was present at the incident.
The High Court refused to quash the proceedings, and the accused appealed that refusal.
issues.conclusion: The proceedings were not fit to be quashed, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure preserves a broad but sparingly exercised inherent power to give effect to orders under the Code, prevent abuse of process, and secure the ends of justice. A court considering quashing may assess whether the allegations, taken at face value, disclose the ingredients of an offence, but must not conduct a trial, assess the reliability of evidence, or decide disputed factual defenses. Proceedings may be quashed where the allegations disclose no offence or where a recognized ground for intervention applies. The Court relied on Zandu Pharmaceutical Works Ltd. v. Mohd. Sharful Haque, S.W. Palanitkar v. State of Bihar, M.A.A. Annamali v. State of Karnataka, Sharda Prasad Sinha v. State of Bihar, Smt. Nagawwa v. Veeranna Shivlingappa Konjalgi, Dharampal v. Smt. Ramshri, State of Haryana v. Bhajanlal, Dhanalakshmi v. R. Prasanna Kumar, and State of Karnataka v. L. Muniswamy.

predicates.appeal_from_refusal_to_quash: The accused appealed after a court refused to quash pending criminal proceedings.
predicates.complaint_alleges_conduct_matching_offen: The complainant alleged conduct that, taken at face value and with the supporting material, corresponds to the elements of the offences alleged.
predicates.defense_depends_on_disputed_facts: The accused relied on contested matters, such as presence at the incident or alleged false implication, that require evidence to resolve.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a refusal to quash, the complaint alleges conduct matching offence elements, and the defense depends on disputed facts, the criminal proceedings are not quashed.
